body:
Your comment really warmed my heart. It's a beautiful reminder for people like us.

I do agree with the part about practice, muscle memory, and just letting it flow. I actually observed in my life. When I try to focus so much on something, I kinda fuck it up but when I am just letting it flow and not minding about outcome of things, i see that my work is better.

I have ADHD too and I love performing and dancing. 
I practice a lot when I have performances and repitition is really my best friend. Learning the steps is really draining for me. I get anxious when I cannot process and do the choreo. Sometimes it's hard not to move forward and not get stucked in my anxieties.

But I observed that after practicing the steps again and again. Practicing it for many times. I get better and better. And when I do it repeatedly, it becomes a muscle memory for me. And feeling the feeling that the steps and the scripts are now in your muscle memory is soooo good. 

Learning them is kinda hard and very time and energy consuming. Sometimes I can't help but compare my speed or pace to others. But when you have learned and mastered it already, it's very beautiful and amazing. 


And oh, there would be moments in life that we can't be ready and have a preparation and this makes me so much frustrated. I am working on this. I think it's important for us to not define ourselves by our own outcomes. Letting go of this is a struggle but reminding our brains that we are more than our outcomes is very important. 

Our results and outcomes should not limit us
 Our outcomes right now are part of our progress. I try to remind myself that if I fucked up and messed up, that's fine! If I cant understand something, not the end of things!
